title: Japanese Pork Dumplings with Zesty Dipping Sauce
description: A classic Japanese dish where pan-seared pork dumplings are served with a zesty dipping sauce made from soy sauce and vinegar.
instructions: In a large pan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil over medium-high heat.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and ginger to the pan and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the liquid has almost completely evaporated.
Let the pork mixture cool slightly.
To assemble the dumplings, lay a dumpling wrapper on a clean surface and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edge of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a half-moon shape, pressing the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
When the oil is hot, add the dumplings to the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, until they are golden brown.
Serve the dumplings hot with a side of zesty dipping sauce (see below).
To make the dipping sauce, combine 1/4 cup of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of vinegar, 1/4 teaspoon of sugar, and 1/4 teaspoon of grated ginger in a small bowl.
Mix the ingredients together until well combined.
